mainTopic: Why טבילה is allowed on שבת and יום הכפורים, whether רבא holds הואיל, and how the משנה about השקה and immersing vessels on יום טוב fits רבי and the חכמים.
overview: The גמרא finishes defending the idea that טבילה on שבת is allowed because it looks like ordinary bathing. People bathe even in smelly מי משרה during a heat wave, and even in winter to wash off mud. On יום הכפורים, when ordinary bathing is forbidden, רבא says that nothing allowed on שבת is forbidden on יום הכפורים. This is reasoning of הואיל ('since'). The גמרא asks whether רבא really holds הואיל, because in the vinegar-for-toothache case he split before dipping from after dipping. It answers that רבא retracted his vinegar ruling, and a ברייתא confirms that required טבילה is done even on תשעה באב and יום הכפורים. Then a new topic begins. שמואל explains that the משנה forbids immersing an impure vessel through its water on יום טוב, while השקה of water in a stone vessel is allowed. The גמרא asks whose view this is, since רבי forbids both and the חכמים permit both. It answers that the משנה can follow רבי, whose ban on השקה applies only on שבת. The way the משנה fits the חכמים comes on the next amud.

steps.title: People bathe even in smelly water on a hot day
steps.stepSummary: This finishes an answer that began on the previous amud. A person might bathe in a heat wave even in foul flax-soaking water, so טבילה in such water still looks like cooling off.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Sometimes a person comes in] during a heat wave and washes himself even in water used for soaking flax.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer to a question asked on the previous amud: how can immersing in bad, smelly water look like cooling off? The answer is that in a heat wave, people bathe even in disgusting flax water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea of נראה כמיקר ('he looks like he is cooling off') only works if an onlooker could believe the person is bathing for comfort. The challenge was that nobody bathes in foul water for comfort. The answer is that real heat makes people bathe in any water at all, so even here an onlooker would not assume he is fixing his טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: A heat wave; intense, oppressive heat
Water in which flax was soaked; foul-smelling, unpleasant water

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the END of an answer whose beginning is on the previous section of the דף. It is not a new statement. It answers 'what about bad water?'

phrases.english: in a heat wave, and washes himself even in flax-soaking water.
phrases.notes: Finishes the sentence 'Sometimes a person comes in…' on the previous amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a defense, begun on the previous amud, of the 'looks like cooling off' explanation against the case of bad water.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Realistic behavior: people really do bathe in bad water when very hot.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Immersing in foul water clearly shows the purpose is טהרה, since nobody would bathe there for pleasure.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a heat wave people bathe even in foul water, so it still looks like cooling off.

steps.title: But what about the rainy season?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the 'cooling off' explanation works in summer, but in winter nobody bathes to cool down.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well in the summer. But in the rainy season, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new objection to the 'cooling off' explanation. In winter nobody bathes to escape heat, so טבילה in winter should look like fixing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heat-wave answer depends on hot weather. In the rainy, cold season the onlooker has no reason to think he is cooling off. So the whole explanation seems to fail for half the year.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This works out fine' — it grants one case before challenging another
'What is there to say?' — a formula for a challenge

phrases.english: This works well in the summer season;
in the rainy season, what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח בִּימוֹת הַחַמָּה, בִּימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the heat-wave answer, then points to a season where heat does not apply.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'נראה כמיקר' (looks like cooling off) explanation for allowing טבילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cooling off only makes sense in hot weather. In winter, bathing shows a purpose of טהרה, which looks like fixing.

steps.title: People wash off mud and filth even in winter
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that people come home from the field dirty and bathe even in winter, so טבילה still looks like ordinary washing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Sometimes a person comes from the field dirty with mud and excrement, and he washes even in the rainy season.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the winter objection. Even in winter people bathe, to get clean after getting filthy in the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for bathing changes from cooling off to cleaning off, but the point stays the same. An onlooker can always think the bather has an ordinary, non-טהרה reason. So the טבילה does not clearly look like fixing.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the answer here

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
Sometimes a person comes from the field
soiled with mud and excrement,
and washes even in the rainy season.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: פְּעָמִים שֶׁאָדָם בָּא מִן הַשָּׂדֶה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative ordinary motive: cleaning instead of cooling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In winter, bathing can only be for טהרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: People bathe in winter to remove dirt, so טבילה still looks like ordinary washing.

steps.title: But what about יום הכפורים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: on שבת bathing is allowed, so טבילה can look like ordinary washing. But on יום הכפורים all bathing is forbidden, so any immersion clearly shows it is for טהרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well on שבת. But on יום הכפורים, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a third objection. On יום הכפורים nobody bathes for comfort or cleanliness, since רחיצה is forbidden, so a person immersing is clearly doing it for טהרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole 'looks like ordinary bathing' answer needs ordinary bathing to be something people do that day. On יום הכפורים ordinary bathing is forbidden, so the cover story disappears. Then טבילה should look like fixing, and it should be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The Day of Atonement, when bathing for pleasure is forbidden
The Sabbath, when bathing itself is not forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not that טבילה is a מלאכה on יום הכפורים. The question is that on יום הכפורים the 'he's just bathing' excuse no longer works, because regular bathing is forbidden.

phrases.english: This works well on Shabbat;
on Yom Kippur, what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח בְּשַׁבָּת, בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same 'תינח… מאי איכא למימר' pattern to move from seasons to a special day.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'looks like ordinary bathing' explanation, as applied to יום הכפורים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On יום הכפורים ordinary bathing is forbidden, so any immersion clearly shows a טהרה purpose and looks like fixing.

steps.title: What is allowed on שבת is allowed on יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that nothing is permitted on שבת yet forbidden on יום הכפורים. Since טבילה is allowed on שבת, it is allowed on יום הכפורים too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Is there anything that is permitted on שבת but forbidden on יום הכפורים? Rather, since it is permitted on שבת, it is permitted on יום הכפורים as well.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the יום הכפורים objection. He does not find a new excuse for the bather. Instead he gives a general rule: יום הכפורים is never stricter than שבת in these matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא admits that on יום הכפורים the bather may clearly look like he is purifying himself. Still, שבת is the stricter day for מלאכה, so the חכמים would not forbid on יום הכפורים what they allowed on שבת. The permission is carried over from שבת to יום הכפורים, even where the original reason does not fully apply.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the final answer here
'Is there anything…?' — a rhetorical question meaning 'surely not'

steps.whatToRemember: טבילה is allowed on שבת because it looks like cooling off (summer, even in bad water) or cleaning off (winter). On יום הכפורים, רבא allows it anyway, because nothing permitted on שבת is forbidden on יום הכפורים.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a general principle: a גזירה of the חכמים is not applied to יום הכפורים more strictly than to שבת. So טבילה stays permitted on יום הכפורים, even where it obviously looks like it is done for טהרה.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Is there anything
that is permitted on Shabbat and prohibited on Yom Kippur?
Rather, since it is permitted on Shabbat —
on Yom Kippur it is also permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִי אִיכָּא מִידֵּי דִּבְשַׁבָּת שְׁרֵי וּבְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the יום הכפורים objection with a structural rule instead of a new practical excuse.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Structural principle: יום הכפורים is not stricter than שבת, so the permission carries over.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since on יום הכפורים the immersion clearly looks like fixing, it should be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because טבילה is permitted on שבת, the חכמים did not forbid it on יום הכפורים, the less strict day for מלאכה.

steps.title: Does רבא really use 'since'? The toothache and vinegar case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבא really holds of הואיל. It begins by quoting a משנה about vinegar for a toothache on שבת, and the ברייתא that seems to contradict it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבא really hold of 'since'? But we learned in a משנה: someone whose teeth hurt may not sip vinegar through them on שבת. He may dip his food in vinegar the normal way, and if it heals him, it heals him. And we raised a contradiction from a ברייתא: one may not sip and spit out, but one may sip and swallow!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a challenge against רבא's 'since' argument from the previous step. This step only sets up the background case; the actual punch of the question comes a few steps later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to ban sipping vinegar entirely. The ברייתא allows sipping if he swallows, because then it looks like normal drinking. The גמרא is reminding us of this old contradiction because of how רבא resolved it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Since': the reasoning that because something is permitted in one case, it is permitted in a related case too
Someone who has pain in his teeth
And we raised a contradiction against it

steps.confusionAlert: The question 'ומי אית ליה לרבא הואיל' is the real challenge. Everything after it is only background that sets up the challenge. The challenge is finished in step 9.

phrases.english: And does Rava hold of 'since'?
phrases.notes: This refers to his argument: since טבילה is allowed on שבת, it is allowed on יום הכפורים.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a mishnah:
One who has pain in his teeth
may not sip vinegar through them (on Shabbat),
phrases.notes: Healing activities are restricted on שבת.

phrases.english: but he may dip his food in his usual way,
and if he is healed, he is healed.
And we raised a contradiction against it:
One may not sip and spit out,
but one may sip and swallow!
phrases.notes: This seems to permit sipping, unlike the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the הואיל reasoning that רבא used in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's use of הואיל to permit טבילה on יום הכפורים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Elsewhere רבא seems to reject הואיל. The full attack is spelled out in step 9.

steps.title: אביי's answer: the משנה means sipping and spitting
steps.stepSummary: אביי resolved the contradiction by reading the משנה as banning only sipping and spitting out.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי said: when we learned the משנה too, we learned it about someone who sips and spits out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא recalls אביי's old answer to the vinegar contradiction. The משנה and the ברייתא agree: sipping and spitting is forbidden, and sipping and swallowing is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי there is no real contradiction. Swallowing looks like normal drinking, so it is permitted at any time. This answer needs no line between before and after dipping.

keyTerms.meaning: אביי, an אמורא and the frequent debating partner of רבא
When we learned it too (it also meant this)

phrases.english: And Abaye said:
When we learned the mishnah too,
we learned it about one who sips and spits out.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר אַבָּיֵי: כִּי תְּנַן נָמֵי מַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the first answer to the contradiction raised in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case in the משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה forbids only sipping and spitting out.

steps.title: רבא's answer: before dipping versus after dipping
steps.stepSummary: רבא answered that even sipping and swallowing is split: it is allowed before dipping and forbidden after dipping.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: you can even say the משנה is about sipping and swallowing, and there is still no difficulty. Here (the ברייתא) is before dipping; there (the משנה) is after dipping.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא recalls רבא's different answer to the vinegar contradiction. This is the answer that will be used against him in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before he dips food, sipping looks like enjoying the vinegar, so it is allowed. After he has already dipped, sipping more clearly looks like medicine, so it is forbidden. רבא treats the two times differently instead of saying one permits the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Here... there (each source is about a different situation)

phrases.english: And Rava said:
Even if you say it is about sipping and swallowing,
it is not difficult:
here (the baraita) is before dipping,
there (the mishnah) is after dipping.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא מְגַמֵּעַ וּבוֹלֵעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, competing answer to the same contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two sources into two different situations
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sipping and swallowing is either always permitted or always forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sipping is permitted before dipping and forbidden after dipping.

steps.title: If רבא holds 'since', he should allow sipping after dipping too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes its challenge. If רבא really held הואיל, he would have said that since sipping is allowed before dipping, it is allowed after dipping too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is so (that רבא holds הואיל), let him say: since it is permitted before dipping, it is also permitted after dipping!
steps.whatsHappening: This is where the challenge from step 6 finally lands. רבא's vinegar answer seems to reject the הואיל reasoning that he used for טבילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the vinegar case, רבא let the same act be permitted at one time and forbidden at another. In the טבילה case, he said 'since it is permitted on שבת, it is permitted on יום הכפורים.' These two positions seem inconsistent.

phrases.english: And if it is so, let him say:
since before dipping it is permitted,
after dipping it is also permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבא's vinegar answer from step 8 to complete the challenge opened in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's consistency: הואיל for טבילה (step 5) versus no הואיל for vinegar (step 8)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If הואיל is valid, it should also have permitted sipping after dipping. רבא did not say this, so it seems he does not hold הואיל.

steps.title: רבא took back his vinegar answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבא retracted his vinegar distinction.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא retracted from that one (the vinegar answer).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the inconsistency by saying רבא changed his mind about the vinegar case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once רבא drops the before-and-after split, he can hold הואיל without contradiction. He would then agree with אביי's reading of the vinegar sources.

keyTerms.meaning: From that one (the earlier ruling being discussed)

phrases.english: Rava retracted from that one (the vinegar ruling).

steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction of one of the conflicting rulings
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא holds both the vinegar split and the הואיל argument.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא dropped the vinegar split and keeps הואיל.

steps.title: How do we know which ruling רבא took back?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know רבא retracted the vinegar ruling. Perhaps he retracted the הואיל ruling about טבילה instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that he retracted from that one? Perhaps he retracted from this one (the טבילה ruling)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the answer it just gave. Two rulings conflict, so how do we know which one רבא dropped?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'he retracted' fixes the contradiction either way. If he dropped the טבילה ruling, he would no longer hold that טבילה on יום הכפורים is permitted for this reason. The גמרא needs a reason to choose the vinegar ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: From this one (the ruling at hand, about טבילה)

phrases.english: And from where do we know that he retracted from that one (vinegar)?
Perhaps he retracted from this one (immersion on Yom Kippur)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions which ruling the retraction in step 10 applies to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of רבא's two rulings he retracted

steps.title: A ברייתא permits טבילה on תשעה באב and יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: רבא could not have dropped the טבילה ruling, because a ברייתא explicitly permits טבילה on תשעה באב and on יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: That cannot enter your mind, for it was taught in a ברייתא: all who are required to immerse do so in their normal way, both on תשעה באב and on יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that רבא kept his טבילה ruling. A ברייתא openly agrees with it, so the ruling he dropped must have been the vinegar one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's conclusion about טבילה matches a ברייתא, and an אמורא would not retract from a position that a ברייתא supports. So the vinegar split is the one he gave up. This confirms the הואיל reasoning and the practical rule that טבילה is allowed on fast days when bathing is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: It cannot enter your mind (that is impossible)
For it was taught in a ברייתא
Those who are required to immerse
The fast of the Ninth of Av, when bathing is forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: רבא holds הואיל: since טבילה is permitted on שבת, it is permitted on יום הכפורים. A ברייתא confirms that the required טבילה is done normally even on תשעה באב and יום הכפורים. רבא's vinegar distinction (before versus after dipping) was retracted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule that a required טבילה is not blocked by the ban on bathing on יום הכפורים and תשעה באב.

phrases.english: That cannot enter your mind,
for it was taught in a baraita:
All who are required to immerse, immerse in their normal way,
whether on Tisha B'Av
or on Yom Kippur.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11 with a ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Perhaps רבא dropped his טבילה ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: The טבילה ruling is backed by a ברייתא, so רבא dropped the vinegar ruling.
steps.raayaObject: That טבילה is permitted on יום הכפורים
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: כל חייבי טבילות טובלין כדרכן בין בתשעה באב בין ביום הכפורים
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא holds הואיל, and required טבילה is permitted on יום הכפורים and תשעה באב.

steps.title: What does 'but one may not immerse' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about השקה in a stone vessel and asks what its closing words 'but one may not immerse' mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And they agree that one may bring water into contact in a stone vessel, etc.' What does 'but one may not immerse' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic. It quotes a line from the משנה and asks what its last words mean, which sets up שמואל's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows השקה: impure water sits in a stone vessel, and the vessel is lowered into a מקוה so the water touches the מקוה water. A stone vessel cannot become impure, so only the water is being purified. The words 'but one may not immerse' are unclear, because they do not say what is being immersed.

keyTerms.meaning: And they agree (בית שמאי and בית הלל)
Bringing impure water into contact with מקוה water to purify it (השקה)
A stone vessel, which cannot become impure

phrases.english: And they agree that one may bring the water into contact
in a stone vessel, etc.
phrases.notes: A stone vessel cannot become impure, so only the water needs purifying

phrases.english: What is 'but one may not immerse'?
phrases.notes: The גמרא asks what exactly is forbidden to immerse

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section. The earlier discussion of רבא and הואיל is finished.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What action the משנה's phrase 'but one may not immerse' forbids.

steps.title: שמואל: no immersing an impure vessel along with its water
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that one may not immerse an impure vessel through its water in order to purify the vessel on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: One may not immerse the vessel by means of its water to purify it on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question. The forbidden immersion is when an impure vessel (not a stone one) holds water and is dipped, which purifies the vessel itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In השקה with a stone vessel, only the water becomes pure. If the vessel can become impure, dipping it purifies the vessel too, and fixing a vessel on יום טוב is not allowed. So the משנה draws the line between purifying water, which is permitted, and purifying a vessel, which is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: By means of its water, meaning the vessel is purified together with the water inside it

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
One may not immerse the vessel
by means of its water
phrases.notes: An impure vessel full of water is dipped so the water touches the מקוה

phrases.english: to purify it on a Festival.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה forbids immersing an impure vessel through its water to purify the vessel on יום טוב. השקה of water in a stone vessel stays permitted.

steps.title: The משנה seems to match neither רבי nor the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: whose view is the משנה? A ברייתא shows that רבי forbids both actions and the חכמים permit both.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is our משנה? Not רבי and not the חכמים. As a ברייתא teaches: One may not immerse a vessel through its water to purify it, and one may not do השקה of water in a stone vessel to purify it. These are the words of רבי. The חכמים say: One may immerse a vessel through its water to purify it, and one may do השקה of water in a stone vessel to purify it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה as שמואל explained it. It brings a ברייתא where both sides treat השקה and הטבלה the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה splits the two actions: השקה is allowed and הטבלה is forbidden. In the ברייתא, רבי forbids both and the חכמים allow both. So no known opinion seems to give the משנה's split result.

keyTerms.meaning: These are the words of רבי (יהודה הנשיא)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two actions. השקה purifies only water, inside a stone vessel. הטבלה על גב מימיו purifies an impure vessel, along with its water.

phrases.english: Whose is our Mishnah?
Not Rabbi and not the Rabbis,
as it is taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַטְבִּילִין אֶת הַכְּלִי עַל גַּב מֵימָיו לְטַהֲרוֹ,
phrases.english: one may not immerse the vessel by means of its water to purify it,
and one may not bring the water into contact
in a stone vessel to purify them,
the words of Rabbi.
And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: מַטְבִּילִין כְּלִי עַל גַּב מֵימָיו לְטַהֲרוֹ,
phrases.english: one may immerse a vessel by means of its water to purify it,
and one may bring the water into contact
in a stone vessel to purify them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי מַתְנִיתִין? לָא רַבִּי וְלָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה as explained by שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: Our משנה, which permits השקה but forbids הטבלה (according to שמואל).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא, each side treats the two actions alike. A משנה that splits them seems to match no one.

steps.title: Pinpointing the clash with each side
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה follows רבי, its ruling on השקה is a problem. If it follows the חכמים, its ruling on הטבלה is a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is it? If רבי's, השקה is difficult. If the חכמים's, immersion is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the challenge exactly. It shows which half of the משנה clashes with each opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי forbids השקה, but the משנה allows it. The חכמים allow הטבלה, but the משנה forbids it. Each possible author leaves one half of the משנה unexplained.

keyTerms.meaning: Touching impure water to מקוה water

phrases.english: Whose is it?
If Rabbi, contact is difficult,
phrases.notes: רבי forbids השקה, but the משנה permits it

phrases.english: if the Rabbis, immersion is difficult!
phrases.notes: The חכמים permit הטבלה, but the משנה forbids it

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי קַשְׁיָא הַשָּׁקָה, אִי רַבָּנַן קַשְׁיָא הַטְבָּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the exact clash behind the challenge of step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: Each half of the משנה, compared against each opinion in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Whichever author we choose, one ruling in the משנה contradicts that author.

steps.title: The משנה can follow רבי: one ruling for יום טוב, one for שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה can fit either side. According to רבי, the first part of his statement applies on יום טוב, the second part only on שבת, and the whole משנה deals with יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is רבי. If you want, say it is the חכמים. If you want, say רבי: the first part of the ברייתא is about יום טוב, the last part is about שבת, and the whole משנה is about יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה can match either opinion. It first explains how it matches רבי. The explanation for the חכמים comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's ban on immersing a vessel applies even on יום טוב, which matches the משנה. His ban on השקה applies only on שבת, which is stricter. Since the משנה is about יום טוב, השקה is allowed there, and the משנה fully matches רבי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common גמרא tool. Two rulings in a ברייתא that look like one rule are split into two different settings, here יום טוב and שבת.

phrases.english: If you wish, say Rabbi,
if you wish, say the Rabbis.
If you wish, say Rabbi:
the first clause of the baraita is on a Festival,
phrases.notes: No immersing a vessel, even on יום טוב

phrases.english: and the latter clause is on Shabbat,
phrases.notes: השקה is forbidden only on שבת

phrases.english: and the entire Mishnah is on a Festival.
phrases.notes: So on יום טוב השקה is permitted and הטבלה is forbidden, matching רבי

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבִּי, אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 15 and 16, starting with the version that follows רבי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the ברייתא's two clauses between יום טוב and שבת.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי forbids both actions in the same setting, so the משנה cannot follow him.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי forbids immersing a vessel even on יום טוב but forbids השקה only on שבת. So a משנה about יום טוב fits רבי.
